clue.text: One might give curls to bust, capturing Pliny's head

definitions.text: One might give curls to bust, capturing Pliny's head

indicators.note: capturing says the shuffled letters close around the next piece
bust means broken, so the letters of curls to are smashed up and rearranged
head picks out the first letter of Pliny's

explanation.surface: A craftsman carving a bust adds curls, perhaps to a head of the Roman writer Pliny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' turns CURLS TO into SCULTOR, and 'capturing' puts P from 'Pliny's head' inside it. The whole clue also describes the answer: a carver adds curls to a bust such as Pliny's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver of statues is the person who would chisel hair curls onto a stone bust.

clue.text: Most interesting bit about capital city? Vote

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
Lima is the capital of Peru
a voter marks a ballot with an X

explanation.surface: Asking whether the high point of a story about a capital is the vote held there.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or culmination of a story is the part that holds the most excitement.

clue.text: Certain stars removed from star billing upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actor has been dropped from top billing on the poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' signals letters taken out of 'star billing'; ARBIL sits inside it, and 'upset' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A constellation is a set of stars, and the Scales of the zodiac is one such group.

clue.text: Ends period at home, too short

parts.note: a school term is a period of time
to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: short says the word for too loses its last letter

parts.note: also is a synonym of too

explanation.surface: A school term finishes while staying home, with too little time.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminals are the end points, such as the final stations of a railway line.

clue.text: Former Communist hiding service in Revolution

indicators.note: hiding says the red word conceals the other piece within it

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a communist

indicators.note: in Revolution says the word for service is turned around

parts.note: a rite is a religious service or ceremony

explanation.surface: A one-time Red Army man who dodged military service during the Russian Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Revolution' turns RITE into ETIR, which RED is 'hiding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped working is a one-time or past holder of a job, as in a former teacher.

clue.text: Wound line returned sound

indicators.note: returned says the word for sound is written backwards

parts.note: noise is a sound

explanation.surface: An instruction about a wound and a returning sound, as if on a radio line.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut or injury to body tissue is the medical sense of the word.

clue.text: Luddites used to wreck these towers

definitions.meaning: the Luddites were 19th-century English textile workers who smashed weaving machines
something that towers rises threateningly over you

explanation.surface: Machine-breakers once destroyed these tall structures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towers' looks like a noun for tall buildings, but it is a verb: rises above.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaving frames were the target of the machine-breakers, and to rise ominously above is to hover large over something.

clue.text: Worry in Midlands county raising character from Oz

indicators.note: in says the worry word sits inside the county
in a down clue raising says the county's letters read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, a county in the English Midlands
care is anxiety or worry

explanation.surface: Anxiety in an English county where someone is bringing up a figure from The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns WORCS into SCROW, and CARE goes 'in' it. Worcestershire is a county in the west Midlands of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The straw man who joins Dorothy on the yellow brick road is a figure in The Wizard of Oz.

clue.text: Countermand order I've set in motion

indicators.note: set in motion says the letters of order I've are moved about

explanation.surface: Cancelling an instruction that one has just started.
explanation.definitionFit: To countermand an order is to cancel or overrule it with a superior authority.

clue.text: Maybe clock frames black and wooden

indicators.note: frames says the timer word surrounds the other letter

parts.note: a clock is one kind of timer, hence maybe
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A clock that perhaps has black wooden frames.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a modifier, as in a timber house, the word means made of wood.

clue.text: Hammer-wielder cleaves chests

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god who wields the hammer Mjolnir
to cleave is to split, as one axes wood

explanation.surface: A hammer-wielding man splits open some wooden chests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chests' looks like boxes being broken, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the part of the body between neck and abdomen, the chest in plural form.

clue.text: Incautious having wine and pork pie before run …

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine
pork pie is cockney rhyming slang for a lie
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone careless enough to have wine and a pork pie before going running.
explanation.walkthrough: In rhyming slang 'pork pie' rhymes with 'lie', so it means a lie; a pork pie is also a British cold meat pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand and careless, showing no proper caution.

clue.text: … start to study unopened red wine

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of study
unopened says the word for red loses its first letter

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a student opens nothing but red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Jerez in southern Spain, commonly drunk as an aperitif.

clue.text: Swine problematic for dated government body

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

indicators.note: problematic says the letters of for dated are put in a troubled order

explanation.surface: A pig is a problem for an outdated ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a British government committee overseeing commerce, now merged into a department.

clue.text: Rollercoaster beginning to buckle, one gripped tight

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of buckle

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, so the letters of gripped are reeling about

explanation.surface: A rider on a fairground ride starts to buckle and holds on tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like how one grips, but as 'drunk' it is the anagram signal turning GRIPPED into GDIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the classic name for a large fairground roller coaster ride.

clue.text: Definitely not forget after pilots picked up father

indicators.note: after says the word for forget comes behind the preceding pieces
in a down clue picked up says the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, whose pilots fly its planes
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to omit something is to forget to include it

explanation.surface: A father is told to forget it once some pilots have collected him.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' means read upward, so backwards; 'after' places the word for forget last, behind the father.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic denial phrase meaning not at all, the very opposite of the case.

clue.text: Left a stone erected topped with huge stone

indicators.note: in a down clue erected says the letters stand upward, read backwards

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

indicators.note: topped says the word with loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A standing stone was left upright, crowned with an even bigger one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns L A GEM upward into MEGAL; 'topped' cuts WITH to ITH. The second 'stone' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalith is a very large stone used in prehistoric monuments such as Stonehenge.

clue.text: Bird moves gradually, quietly in distress

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the word for distress

parts.note: to harrow is to distress or torment
to edge is to move gradually
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A small bird creeps along quietly because it is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the dunnock, a small brown songbird common in British hedgerows.

clue.text: Judge a bishop eating snack

indicators.note: eating says the bishop's letters surround the snack

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: A judge and a bishop share a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone whose word settles a dispute, as a referee or adjudicator does.

clue.text: Feel hot carrying heartless duke's cargo

indicators.note: carrying says the hot word holds the cut duke within it

parts.note: to burn is to feel hot

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letters of duke are removed

parts.note: the word duke is taken here and cut

explanation.surface: A worker sweating while hauling a weakened duke's cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A load carried, especially a heavy one, is the original sense of a burden.

clue.text: Sending communication to team occupying one of the choppers

indicators.note: occupying says the team sits inside the tooth

parts.note: choppers is slang for teeth, and a fang is a tooth
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Messaging a team aboard one of the helicopters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppers' suggests helicopters, but it is slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Faxing a document transmits a copy over a telephone line, a way of sending a message.

clue.text: Soiled golf skirt on yard

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a rim is an edge, the skirt of something

explanation.surface: A golfer's skirt got dirty in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimy describes something covered with ingrained dirt.

clue.text: Lovers receiving gold, diamonds and booze

indicators.note: receiving says the lovers take the other letters inside

parts.note: beaux are boyfriends or admirers
or is gold in heraldry
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Suitors are given gold, diamonds and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from the region around Bordeaux in France, here as a casual word for alcohol.

clue.text: Free entry regularly accessed by politician

indicators.note: accessed by says the politician gets into the picked letters
regularly picks every other letter of entry

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Free admission is often taken advantage of by a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to free a container is to clear it out, leaving nothing in it.

clue.text: Exactly identify amount of fluid collecting in river

indicators.note: collecting says the measure gathers the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a pint is a measure of liquid
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: Measuring the precise volume of water gathered in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate or name something with complete precision, as on a map.

clue.text: Was down south to find vehicles

parts.note: to mope is to be down in spirits, so moped means was down

explanation.surface: Someone was depressed going south looking for cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was down' reads as a verb phrase; MOPED is the past tense of mope, but also the light motorcycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopeds are small, low-powered motorbikes, a kind of road transport.

clue.text: Ill-tempered figure has succeeded for first time

indicators.note: for first time says the new letter replaces the first T of the figure

parts.note: thirty is a figure, a number
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A grumpy person has succeeded for the first time, at the age of thirty perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shirty' is informal British for cross or bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirty is British slang for annoyed and irritable, quick to lose one's temper.

clue.text: Again hearing tyre needs replacing in call

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters go inside the word for call

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

indicators.note: needs replacing says the letters of tyre are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A garage call: hearing again that the tyre must be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs replacing' turns TYRE into ETRY, put 'in' RING. 'hearing' is the court sense: a case heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that hears a case a second time is putting it on trial anew.
